```{r}
# Load required library
library(dplyr)
library(pheatmap)

# Specify variables to exclude
exclude_vars <- c("Age", "Gender", "Metabolic_Syndrome_IDF", "WHO_BMI_Category", "WHR_Category", "Diabetes_WHO", "Hypertension")

# Rename columns using dplyr
Data.soft <- Data.soft %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Age = u3talteru, 
    Gender = u3csex, 
    Weight = u3tgewi, 
    Height = u3tgroe, 
    BMI = u3tbmi,
    WHO_BMI_Category = u3tbmiwho,  
    WHR = u3twhrat,  
    WHR_Category = u3twhratc, 
    SBP = u3tsysmm, 
    DBP = u3tdiamm, 
    Hypertension = u3twhoish,  
    Fasting_glucose = u3tglukfastn,  
    Glucose_2h = u3tgluk2n,  
    Diabetes_WHO = u3tdm110y15,  
    Fasting_serum_insulin = u3tinsfastn,  
    Insulin_2h = u3tins2n,  
    Metabolic_Syndrome_IDF = u3tmsidfup,  
    HOMA_Beta = u3thoma2_b,  
    HOMA_Sensitivity = u3thoma2_s,  
    HOMA_IR = u3thoma2_ir,  
    Insulin_Sensitivity_Quicki = u3tquickin,
    Cholesterol = u3lk_choln,  
    HDL = u3lk_hdln, 
    LDL = u3lk_ldln,  
    TG = u3lk_trin, 
    Creatinine = u3lk_krean, 
    HbA1c = u3l_hbavn,   
    hsCRP = u3h_crp
  )

# Get the variable names to use (exclude the specified variables)
all_vars <- colnames(Data.soft)
vars_to_use <- setdiff(all_vars, exclude_vars)

# Keep only numeric columns
numeric_vars <- vars_to_use[sapply(Data.soft[, vars_to_use], is.numeric)]
Data.analysis <- Data.soft[, numeric_vars]


# Initialize matrices
n_vars <- length(vars_to_use)
mw_p_values <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_vars, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))
median_diff_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_vars, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))

# Perform Mann-Whitney U test and calculate median difference (as effect direction)
for (i in 1:n_vars) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(adjusted_assignments)) {
    group1 <- Data.analysis[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 1, i]
    group2 <- Data.analysis[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 0, i]

    if (length(group1) > 2 && length(group2) > 2) {
      test_result <- wilcox.test(group1, group2, exact = FALSE)
      mw_p_values[i, j] <- test_result$p.value
      # Use median difference as direction
      median_diff_matrix[i, j] <- median(group1, na.rm = TRUE) - median(group2, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
}

# Adjust p-values for multiple comparisons (FDR)
p_values_adjusted <- matrix(p.adjust(mw_p_values, method = "fdr"), 
                            nrow = nrow(mw_p_values), 
                            ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

# Convert adjusted p-values to significance stars
significance_matrix <- matrix(sapply(p_values_adjusted, function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}), nrow = nrow(mw_p_values), ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

# Assign row and column names
rownames(median_diff_matrix) <- rownames(significance_matrix) <- vars_to_use
colnames(median_diff_matrix) <- colnames(significance_matrix) <- colnames(adjusted_assignments)

# Scale for heatmap visualization
scaled_medians <- scale(median_diff_matrix)

# Define heatmap color palette
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)

# Save heatmap
jpeg("Heatmap_MedianDiff_Archetypes.jpeg", width = 1800, height = 1000, res = 300)

pheatmap(scaled_medians, 
         cluster_rows = TRUE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE,
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         color = my_palette,
         main = "Heatmap of Archetypes",
         fontsize_row = 6,
         fontsize_col = 8,
         angle_col = "0",
         border_color = "grey70",
         display_numbers = significance_matrix)

dev.off()
```

#Normalisation 

## inverse-normal transformation of variables(Transforming data into normal data)
### First the categorical variabels should be excluded and the transformation should only be done on the numerical data
### Exclude specific columns and select only numeric columns

```{r}
Data.soft_subset <- Data.soft[, -c(2, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17)]
numeric_cols <- names(Data.soft_subset)[sapply(Data.soft_subset, is.numeric)]  # Get names of numeric columns

#### Apply the transformation to each numeric column in the original Data.soft and then viewing the data 

Data.soft[numeric_cols] <- lapply(Data.soft[numeric_cols], function(col) { 
  qnorm((rank(col, na.last = "keep") - 0.5) / sum(!is.na(col)))
})
```


#Visualisation of Normalised data 
###histgram of only numerical variables 
```{r}
hist(data.matrix(Data.soft[,-c(2, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17)]))

##Shapiro test for checking the normality 

# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)

# Perform Shapiro-Wilk test for normality
shapiro_results <- data.frame(Variable = names(Data.soft)[1:28], p.value = NA)

for (i in 1:28) {
  variable <- Data.soft[, i]
  shapiro_results$p.value[i] <- shapiro.test(variable)$p.value
}

# Display Shapiro-Wilk test results
print(shapiro_results)

# Visual inspection using histograms and Q-Q plots
for (i in 1:28) {
  variable <- Data.soft[, i]
  
  # Histogram
  p <- ggplot(data = Data.soft, aes(x = !!sym(names(Data.soft)[i]))) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5) +
    ggtitle(paste("Histogram of", names(Data.soft)[i])) +
    theme_minimal()
  ggsave(paste0("histogram_", names(Data.soft)[i], ".png"), plot = p)
  
  # Q-Q plot
  png(paste0("qqplot_", names(Data.soft)[i], ".png"))
  qqnorm(variable, main = paste("Q-Q Plot of", names(Data.soft)[i]))
  qqline(variable, col = "red")
  dev.off()
}

```

#Dealing with categorical variables 
```{r}
# Select categorical variables
categorical_cols <- c("u3twhratc", "u3twhoish", "u3tdm110y15", "u3tmsidfup", "u3csex", "u3tbmiwho")


# Convert categorical columns to factors
Data.soft$u3twhratc <- as.factor(Data.soft$u3twhratc)
Data.soft$u3twhoish <- as.factor(Data.soft$u3twhoish)
Data.soft$u3tdm110y15 <- as.factor(Data.soft$u3tdm110y15)
Data.soft$u3tmsidfup <- as.factor(Data.soft$u3tmsidfup)
Data.soft$u3csex <- as.factor(Data.soft$u3csex)
Data.soft$u3tbmiwho <- as.factor(Data.soft$u3tbmiwho)


# Apply one-hot encoding
Data.soft_encoded <- cbind(
  Data.soft[numeric_cols],  # Keep the numeric columns as they are
  model.matrix(~ u3twhratc - 1, data = Data.soft),  # One-hot encode 'u3twhratc'
  model.matrix(~ u3twhoish - 1, data = Data.soft),  # One-hot encode 'u3twhoish'
  model.matrix(~ u3tdm110y15 - 1, data = Data.soft),  # One-hot encode 'u3tdm110y15'
  model.matrix(~ u3tmsidfup - 1, data = Data.soft),  # One-hot encode 'u3tmsidfup'
  model.matrix(~ u3csex - 1, data = Data.soft),  # One-hot encode 'u3csex'
  model.matrix(~ u3tbmiwho - 1, data = Data.soft)  # One-hot encode 'u3tbmiwho'
)

# Now, Data.soft_encoded contains the combined numeric and one-hot encoded categorical variables

save(Data.soft_encoded , file = "Data.soft_encoded.RData")
```

#Descriptive statistics for cartegorical and countinous (not included in the analysis)
```{r}

#CBCgrps package
# Define categorical columns
categorical_cols <- c("u3twhratc", "u3twhoish", "u3tdm110y15", "u3tmsidfup", "u3csex", "u3tbmiwho")

# Convert selected columns to factor type
Data.soft <- Data.soft %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(categorical_cols), as.factor))

# Double-check: Ensure grouping variable is also a factor (optional if included above)
Data.soft$u3tmsidfup <- as.factor(Data.soft$u3tmsidfup)

# Use CBCgrps::twogrps to compare variables by group
Baseline_Characteristics_categorical <- twogrps(Data.soft,
  gvar = "u3tmsidfup",      # Grouping variable (e.g., IDF definition)
  varlist = categorical_cols,  # Variables to summarize
  p.rd = 3,
  skewvar = NULL,
  norm.rd = 2,
  sk.rd = 2,
  tabNA = "no",
  cat.rd = 0,
  pnormtest = 0.0001,
  maxfactorlevels = 30,
  minfactorlevels = 10,
  sim = TRUE,
  workspace = 2e+05,
  ShowStatistic = FALSE,
  ExtractP = 0.05
)

print(Baseline_Characteristics_categorical)
View(Baseline_Characteristics_categorical)


continous_cols <- c("u3talteru","u3tgewi", "u3tgroe", "u3tbmi","u3twhrat",
                    "u3twhratc", "u3tsysmm", "u3tglukfastn", "u3tgluk2n", "u3tinsfastn",
                    "u3tins2n", "u3tquickin", "u3lk_choln", "u3lk_hdln", "u3lk_ldln","u3lk_trin",
                    "u3lk_krean", "u3l_hbavn", "u3h_crp", "u3thoma2_ir","u3thoma2_s", "u3thoma2_b")




# Create a variable for baseline characteristics and specify grouping variables

  cat.rd = 0,  # Rounding for categorical variables

  maxfactorlevels = 30,  # Maximum levels for factors
  minfactorlevels = 10,  # Minimum levels for factors
  sim = TRUE,  # Enable simulation for statistical test
  workspace = 2e+05,  # Workspace size for statistical tests
  ShowStatistic = FALSE,  # Hide test statistics
  ExtractP = 0.05  # Extract significant results (p < 0.05)
)
```

#Checking the stability of archetypes 
```{r}
set.seed(1981)

library(archetypes)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(fossil)
library(tidyr)
cutoff_values <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.05)
k_values <- 1:10
original_assignments_list <- list()

for (k in k_values) {
  original_assignments_list[[k]] <- lapply(cutoff_values, function(cutoff) {
    alphas <- bestModel(as.robust[[k]])$alphas
    apply(alphas > cutoff, 1, function(x) ifelse(any(x), which(x), NA))
  })
}
print("ok - original assignments list created for k = 1 to 10")

calculate_stability <- function(k, cutoff, data, original_assignments, n_iterations = 100) { 
  print(paste("Starting stability calculation for k =", k, "and cutoff =", cutoff))
  rand_indices <- numeric(n_iterations)
  
  for (i in 1:n_iterations) {
    subsample <- sample(nrow(data), size = floor(0.9 * nrow(data)))
    subdata <- data[subsample, ]
    
    submodel <- tryCatch(
      archetypes(subdata, family = archetypesFamily("robust"), k = k),
      error = function(e) {
        print(paste("Error in archetypes:", e$message))
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
    
    if (is.null(submodel)) {
      rand_indices[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    sub_alphas <- coef(submodel, type = "alphas")
    
    if (is.null(sub_alphas) || ncol(sub_alphas) == 0) {
      rand_indices[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    sub_assignments <- apply(sub_alphas > cutoff, 1, function(x) ifelse(any(x), which(x)[1], NA))
    
    if (length(original_assignments[subsample]) == length(sub_assignments)) {
      rand_indices[i] <- adj.rand.index(original_assignments[subsample], sub_assignments)
    } else {
      rand_indices[i] <- NA
    }
  }
  
  return(rand_indices)
}

print("ok - calculate_stability function defined")

# Main calculation loop
stability_results <- expand.grid(k = k_values, cutoff = cutoff_values)
stability_results$iterations <- I(rep(list(numeric(100)), nrow(stability_results)))

for (i in 1:nrow(stability_results)) {
  stability_results$iterations[[i]] <- calculate_stability(
    stability_results$k[i],
    stability_results$cutoff[i],
    Data.soft,
    original_assignments_list[[stability_results$k[i]]][[which(cutoff_values == stability_results$cutoff[i])]]
  )
  
  # Save the mean ARI as well
  stability_results$stability[i] <- mean(stability_results$iterations[[i]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Save results
save(stability_results, file = "robust_stability_results_k1-10.RData")
write.csv(stability_results, "robust_stability_results_k1-10.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r}
  mutate(k = as.factor(k), cutoff = as.factor(cutoff))

# Plot
ggplot(cluster_long, aes(x = k, y = ARI)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "grey80", color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ cutoff, ncol = 4, labeller = label_both) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted Rand Index across Clusters and Cutoff Values (0.2–0.9)",
    x = "Number of Clusters (k)",
    y = "Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)"
  )
ggsave("archeatype-stabilty-different-cutoffs.png", width = 15, height = 10, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("archeatype-stabilty-different-cutoffs.pdf", width = 15, height = 10, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```


#Stability code of Sapna.finalised 
##Sapna has changed the archetypes(subdata, k = k) to  archetypes(subdata, family = archetypesFamily("robust"), k = k)
```{r}
set.seed(1981)
# Precompute original archetypes assignments
cutoff_values <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.05)  # Define multiple cutoff values
original_assignments_list <- lapply(cutoff_values, function(cutoff) {
    alphas <- bestModel(as[[k_value]])$alphas
    apply(alphas > cutoff, 1, function(x) ifelse(any(x), which(x), NA))
})
names(original_assignments_list) = cutoff_values

print("ok - original assignments list created")

calculate_stability <- function(k, cutoff, data, original_assignments, n_iterations = 100) { 
  print(paste("Starting stability calculation for k =", k, "and cutoff =", cutoff))
  rand_indices <- numeric(n_iterations)
  
  for (i in 1:n_iterations) {
    subsample <- sample(nrow(data), size = floor(0.9 * nrow(data)))
    subdata <- data[subsample, ]
    
    # Fit archetypes on subsampled data
    submodel <- tryCatch(
      archetypes(subdata, family = archetypesFamily("robust"), k = k),
      error = function(e) {
        print(paste("Error in archetypes:", e$message))
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
    
    if (is.null(submodel)) {
      print("Submodel is NULL")
      rand_indices[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    sub_alphas <- coef(submodel, type = "alphas")
    
    if (is.null(sub_alphas) || ncol(sub_alphas) == 0) {
      print("sub_alphas is NULL or has 0 columns")
      rand_indices[i] <- NA
      next
    }
    
    # Get original archetypes for comparison
    
    # Get assignments for subsampled data
    sub_assignments <- apply(sub_alphas > cutoff, 1, function(x) ifelse(any(x), which(x)[1], NA))
    
    # Print lengths for debugging
    print(paste("Length of original_assignments[subsample]:", length(original_assignments[subsample])))
    print(paste("Length of sub_assignments:", length(sub_assignments)))
    
    # Check lengths and calculate adjusted Rand index
    if (length(original_assignments[subsample]) == length(sub_assignments)) {
      rand_indices[i] <- adj.rand.index(original_assignments[subsample], sub_assignments)
      print(paste("Iteration", i, "ARI:", rand_indices[i]))
    } else {
      print("Length mismatch in assignments")
      rand_indices[i] <- NA
    }
  }
  
  result <- mean(rand_indices, na.rm = TRUE)
  print(paste("Stability calculation completed. Result:", result))
  return(rand_indices)
  #return(result)
}
print("ok - calculate_stability function defined")

# Main calculation loop
stability_results <- NULL
stability_results <- expand.grid(k = k_value, cutoff = cutoff_values)


coll_stability = NULL
for (i in 1:nrow(stability_results)) {
  stability <- NULL
  stability <- calculate_stability(
    stability_results$k[i],
    stability_results$cutoff[i],
    Data.soft,
    original_assignments_list[[as.character(stability_results$cutoff[i])]]
  )
  coll_stability = rbind(coll_stability,stability)
}

stability_results$mean = rowMeans(coll_stability)
stability_results = cbind(stability_results,coll_stability)

# Save results
write.csv(stability_results, paste0("stability_results_k",k_value,"_sh.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r}
    }
```
```{r}
  }
```
```{r}
}
```

```{r}
combined_data <- cbind(Data.soft[, c(1:28)], adjusted_assignments)
```

#Correlation matrix of pairwise of the countinous variales 
```{r}
#For saving figures
setwd(Sys.getenv("KORA_RUN_DIR"))
# List of columns to exclude
excluded_vars <- c("Age", "Gender", "Metabolic_Syndrome_IDF", "WHO_BMI_Category", 
                   "WHR_Category", "Diabetes_WHO", "Hypertension")

# Keep only numeric columns and remove excluded columns for clinical variables
clinical_vars <- setdiff(colnames(Data.soft), excluded_vars)
clinical_numeric_vars <- clinical_vars[sapply(Data.soft[, clinical_vars, drop=FALSE], is.numeric)]
Data.clinical <- Data.soft[, clinical_numeric_vars, drop=FALSE]

# Compute correlation matrix for only clinical variables vs archetypes
correlation_matrix <- cor(Data.clinical, adjusted_assignments, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Function for significance testing for correlation matrix
cor.mtest <- function(mat, conf.level = 0.95) {
  mat <- as.matrix(mat)
  n <- ncol(mat)
  p.mat <- matrix(NA, n, n)
  
  for (i in 1:n) {
    for (j in 1:n) {
      if (i != j) {  # Avoid redundant diagonal computations
        test <- cor.test(mat[, i], mat[, j], method = "pearson")
        p.mat[i, j] <- test$p.value
      }
    }
  }
  colnames(p.mat) <- rownames(p.mat) <- colnames(mat)
  return(list(p = p.mat))
}

# compute p-values for correlation
cor_test_results <- cor.mtest(correlation_matrix, conf.level = 0.95)

# convert p-values into significance stars, handling NA values
significance_matrix <- matrix(sapply(cor_test_results$p, function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}), nrow = nrow(correlation_matrix), ncol = ncol(correlation_matrix))

# ensure dimensions match before plotting
if (!all(dim(significance_matrix) == dim(correlation_matrix))) {
  stop("Error: Dimensions of significance matrix do not match correlation matrix!")
}
pdf("Corrplot_Fixed-k4.pdf", width = 8, height = 8)
library(corrplot)
corrplot(correlation_matrix, 
         method = "color",       
         tl.col = "black",       
         tl.cex = 1.2,         
         tl.srt = 45,            
         mar = c(5, 6, 4, 8),    # More space for the legend
         cl.ratio = 0.4,         # Make the legend wider
         cl.align.text = "l",    
         cl.cex = 0.8,           # Make legend text larger
         cl.length = 11,         # More ticks on the color bar
         cl.lim = c(-1, 1)       # Ensure legend covers full correlation range
)

dev.off()
```

```{r}
# Function to compute p-values for correlation matrix
cor.mtest <- function(mat, conf.level = 0.95) {
  n <- ncol(mat)
  p.mat <- matrix(NA, n, n)
  colnames(p.mat) <- colnames(mat)
  rownames(p.mat) <- rownames(mat)
  
  for (i in 1:(n - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):n) {
      test <- cor.test(mat[, i], mat[, j], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
```

```{r}
# Load required library
library(pheatmap)

# Initialize matrices
mw_p_values <- matrix(NA, nrow = 28, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))
median_diff_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = 28, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))

# Perform Mann-Whitney U test and calculate median difference (as effect direction)
for (i in 1:28) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(adjusted_assignments)) {
    group1 <- Data.soft[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 1, i]
    group2 <- Data.soft[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 0, i]
    
    if (length(group1) > 2 && length(group2) > 2) {
      test_result <- wilcox.test(group1, group2, exact = FALSE)
      mw_p_values[i, j] <- test_result$p.value
      # Use median difference as direction
      median_diff_matrix[i, j] <- median(group1, na.rm = TRUE) - median(group2, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
}

# Adjust p-values for multiple comparisons (FDR)
p_values_adjusted <- matrix(p.adjust(mw_p_values, method = "fdr"), 
                            nrow = nrow(mw_p_values), 
                            ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

# Convert adjusted p-values to significance stars
significance_matrix <- matrix(sapply(p_values_adjusted, function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}), nrow = nrow(mw_p_values), ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

# Assign row and column names
rownames(median_diff_matrix) <- rownames(significance_matrix) <- colnames(Data.soft[, 1:28])
colnames(median_diff_matrix) <- colnames(significance_matrix) <- colnames(adjusted_assignments)

# Scale for heatmap visualization
scaled_medians <- scale(median_diff_matrix)

# Define heatmap color palette
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)

# Save heatmap
jpeg("Heatmap_MedianDiff_Archetypes.jpeg", width = 1800, height = 1000, res = 300)

pheatmap(scaled_medians, 
         cluster_rows = TRUE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE,
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         color = my_palette,
         main = "Heatmap of Archetypes",
         fontsize_row = 6,
         fontsize_col = 8,
         angle_col = "0",
         border_color = "grey70",
         display_numbers = significance_matrix)

dev.off()
```

```{r}
setwd(Sys.getenv("KORA_RUN_DIR"))

# Load required library
library(pheatmap)
# Rename columns using dplyr
Data.soft <- Data.soft %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Age = u3talteru, 
    Gender = u3csex, 
    Weight = u3tgewi, 
    Height = u3tgroe, 
    BMI = u3tbmi,
    WHO_BMI_Category = u3tbmiwho,  
    WHR = u3twhrat,  
    WHR_Category = u3twhratc, 
    SBP = u3tsysmm, 
    DBP = u3tdiamm, 
    Hypertension = u3twhoish,  
    Fasting_glucose = u3tglukfastn,  
    Glucose_2h = u3tgluk2n,  
    Diabetes_WHO = u3tdm110y15,  
    Fasting_serum_insulin = u3tinsfastn,  
    Insulin_2h = u3tins2n,  
    Metabolic_Syndrome_IDF = u3tmsidfup,  
    HOMA_Beta = u3thoma2_b,  
    HOMA_Sensitivity = u3thoma2_s,  
    HOMA_IR = u3thoma2_ir,  
    Insulin_Sensitivity_Quicki = u3tquickin,
    Cholesterol = u3lk_choln,  
    HDL = u3lk_hdln, 
    LDL = u3lk_ldln,  
    TG = u3lk_trin, 
    Creatinine = u3lk_krean, 
    HbA1c = u3l_hbavn,   
    hsCRP = u3h_crp
  )
#For saving figures
setwd(Sys.getenv("KORA_RUN_DIR"))

# Define variables to exclude
excluded_vars <- c("Age", "Gender", "Metabolic_Syndrome_IDF", "WHO_BMI_Category", "WHR_Category", "Diabetes_WHO", "Hypertension")

# Select variables to include for the heatmap (excluding the specified ones)
included_data_soft <- Data.soft[, !(colnames(Data.soft) %in% excluded_vars)]

# Only keep numeric columns to avoid errors in wilcox.test
included_data_soft <- included_data_soft[, sapply(included_data_soft, is.numeric)]

# Update the number of rows for matrices based on the included variables
num_included_vars <- ncol(included_data_soft)


# Ensure Extreme_Archetype_Number is treated as a character
Data.soft$Extreme_Archetype_Number <- as.character(Data.soft$Extreme_Archetype_Number)

adjusted_assignments <- data.frame(matrix(0, nrow = nrow(Data.soft), ncol = 5))
colnames(adjusted_assignments) <- c("1","2","3","4","Mixed Etiology")

# Fill the adjusted assignments based on Extreme Archetype Number
for (i in 1:nrow(Data.soft)) {
  if (!is.na(Data.soft$Extreme_Archetype_Number[i])) {
    if (Data.soft$Extreme_Archetype_Number[i] == "Mixed Etiology") {
      adjusted_assignments[i, 5] <- 1 # Mixed Etiology
    } else {
      archetype_index <- as.numeric(Data.soft$Extreme_Archetype_Number[i])
      adjusted_assignments[i, archetype_index] <- 1 # Set corresponding archetype to 1
    }
  }
}


# Initialize matrices with the correct dimensions
mw_p_values <- matrix(NA, nrow = num_included_vars, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))
median_diff_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = num_included_vars, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))

# Perform Mann-Whitney U test and calculate median difference (as effect direction)
for (i in 1:num_included_vars) { # Loop through the included variables
  for (j in 1:ncol(adjusted_assignments)) {
    group1 <- included_data_soft[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 1, i]
    group2 <- included_data_soft[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 0, i]

    if (length(group1) > 2 && length(group2) > 2) {
      test_result <- wilcox.test(group1, group2, exact = FALSE)
      mw_p_values[i, j] <- test_result$p.value
      # Use median difference as direction
      median_diff_matrix[i, j] <- median(group1, na.rm = TRUE) - median(group2, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
}

# Adjust p-values for multiple comparisons (FDR)
p_values_adjusted <- matrix(p.adjust(mw_p_values, method = "fdr"),
                            nrow = nrow(mw_p_values),
                            ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

# Convert adjusted p-values to significance stars
significance_matrix <- matrix(sapply(p_values_adjusted, function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}), nrow = nrow(mw_p_values), ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

# Assign row and column names
rownames(median_diff_matrix) <- rownames(significance_matrix) <- colnames(included_data_soft)
colnames(median_diff_matrix) <- colnames(significance_matrix) <- colnames(adjusted_assignments)

# Scale for heatmap visualization
```

```{r}
#compute correlation matrix for only clinical variables vs archetypes
correlation_matrix <- cor(Data.soft[,1:28], adjusted_assignments, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

cor.mtest <- function(mat, conf.level = 0.95) {
  mat <- as.matrix(mat)
  n <- ncol(mat)
  p.mat <- matrix(NA, n, n)
  
  for (i in 1:n) {
    for (j in 1:n) {
      if (i != j) {  # Avoid redundant diagonal computations
        test <- cor.test(mat[, i], mat[, j], method = "pearson")
        p.mat[i, j] <- test$p.value
      }
    }
  }
  colnames(p.mat) <- rownames(p.mat) <- colnames(mat)
  return(list(p = p.mat))
}

#compute p-values for correlation
cor_test_results <- cor.mtest(correlation_matrix, conf.level = 0.95)

#convert p-values into significance stars, handling NA values
significance_matrix <- matrix(sapply(cor_test_results$p, function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")  # Handle NA values gracefully
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}), nrow = nrow(correlation_matrix), ncol = ncol(correlation_matrix))

#nsure dimensions match before plotting
if (!all(dim(significance_matrix) == dim(correlation_matrix))) {
  stop("Error: Dimensions of significance matrix do not match correlation matrix!")
}

# Save heatmap as JPEG
jpeg("Heatmap_of_6_Archetypes_Pearson.jpeg", width = 1800, height = 1000, res = 300)

# Define color palette
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)

# Create heatmap
pheatmap(correlation_matrix, 
         cluster_rows = TRUE,  
         cluster_cols = FALSE,  
         scale = "row",
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         color = my_palette,
         main = "Heatmap of Archetypes",
         fontsize_row = 6,
         fontsize_col = 8, #angle_col = 45,
         angle_col = 0,
         border_color = "grey70",
         display_numbers = significance_matrix)

# Close device to save file
dev.off()
```

```{r}
mw_p_values <- matrix(NA, nrow = 28, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))
mw_test_estimates <- matrix(NA, nrow = 28, ncol = ncol(adjusted_assignments))

# Perform Mann-Whitney U test for each clinical variable vs. each archetype group
for (i in 1:28) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(adjusted_assignments)) {
    group1 <- Data.soft[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 1, i]  # Selected archetype group
    group2 <- Data.soft[adjusted_assignments[, j] == 0, i]  # Remaining individuals
    
    if (length(group1) > 2 && length(group2) > 2) {  # Ensure enough data points
      test_result <- wilcox.test(group1, group2, exact = FALSE)  # Mann-Whitney U test
      mw_p_values[i, j] <- test_result$p.value
      mw_test_estimates[i, j] <- median(group1, na.rm = TRUE) - median(group2, na.rm = TRUE)  # Directionality
    }
  }
}

# Adjust p-values for multiple comparisons
p_values_adjusted <- matrix(p.adjust(mw_p_values, method = "fdr"), nrow = nrow(mw_p_values), ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

# Convert p-values into significance stars
significance_matrix <- matrix(sapply(p_values_adjusted, function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")  
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}), nrow = nrow(mw_p_values), ncol = ncol(mw_p_values))

rownames(scaled_estimates) <- rownames(mw_test_estimates) <- colnames(Data.soft[, 1:28])  # Clinical variable names
colnames(scaled_estimates) <- colnames(mw_test_estimates) <- colnames(adjusted_assignments)  # Archetype group names
rownames(significance_matrix) <- rownames(mw_test_estimates)
colnames(significance_matrix) <- colnames(mw_test_estimates)


# Scale test estimates for visualization (keeping directionality)
scaled_estimates <- scale(mw_test_estimates)

# Define heatmap color palette (red = higher, blue = lower)
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)

# Save heatmap as JPEG
jpeg("Heatmap_of_6_Archetypes_Mann-whitey.jpeg", width = 1800, height = 1000, res = 300)

# Create heatmap
pheatmap(scaled_estimates, 
         cluster_rows = TRUE,  
         cluster_cols = FALSE,  
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         color = my_palette,
         main = "Heatmap of Clinical Variables vs Archetypes",
         fontsize_row = 6,
         fontsize_col = 8,
         angle_col = 0,
         border_color = "grey70",
         display_numbers = significance_matrix)

# Close graphics device
dev.off()
```

#Creating Heatmap of Mixed Etiology using the Linear regression
```{r}
#Defining  the clinical variables for analysis
clinical_vars <- c("u3talteru", "u3csex", "u3tgewi", "u3tgroe", "u3tbmi", 
                                                  "u3tbmiwho", "u3twhrat", "u3twhratc", "u3tsysmm", 
                                                  "u3tdiamm", "u3twhoish", "u3tglukfastn", 
                                                  "u3tgluk2n", "u3tdm110y15", "u3tinsfastn", 
                                                  "u3tins2n", "u3tmsidfup", "u3tquickin",  
                                                  "u3lk_choln", "u3lk_hdln", "u3lk_ldln", 
                                                  "u3lk_trin", "u3lk_krean", "u3l_hbavn", 
                                                  "u3h_crp", "u3thoma2_ir","u3thoma2_s", "u3thoma2_b")


Data.soft$Mixed_Group <- NA
Data.soft$Mixed_Group[mixed_etiology] <- mixed_groups

#  Initialize matrices to store test estimates and p-values
test_estimates <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(clinical_vars), ncol = length(unique(mixed_groups)))
p_values <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(clinical_vars), ncol = length(unique(mixed_groups)))

rownames(test_estimates) <- clinical_vars
colnames(test_estimates) <- unique(mixed_groups)
rownames(p_values) <- clinical_vars
colnames(p_values) <- unique(mixed_groups)
for (group in unique(mixed_groups)) {
  group_indices <- which(Data.soft$Mixed_Group == group)
  
  for (var in clinical_vars) {
    if (!is.null(group_indices) && length(group_indices) > 0) {
      Data.soft$group_member <- ifelse(Data.soft$Mixed_Group == group, 1, 0)
      
      # Run linear regression (considering the clinical variable as continuous)
      model <- lm(Data.soft[[var]] ~ Data.soft$group_member)
      test_estimates[var, group] <- coef(model)[2]  # Coefficient for group membership
      p_values[var, group] <- summary(model)$coefficients[2, 4]  # p-value
    }
  }
}
get_significance <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}

# Apply the significance function to p-values
significance <- matrix(sapply(p_values, get_significance), nrow = nrow(p_values))
rownames(significance) <- rownames(test_estimates)
colnames(significance) <- colnames(test_estimates)

my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)
pheatmap((test_estimates), 
         cluster_rows = FALSE,  # Perform clustering on rows (samples)
         cluster_cols = FALSE,  # Perform clustering on columns (metabolites)
         scale = "row", # Scale rows for better visualization
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         display_numbers = significance, 
         color = my_palette,
         angle_col = 0,#0 for horizontal, 45 for rotation andfor vertical 90
         main = "Heatmap of Clinical Associations Across Mixed Etiology Groups")

```

```{r}
      group1 <- Data.soft[[var]][Data.soft$Mixed_Group == group]
      group2 <- Data.soft[[var]][Data.soft$Mixed_Group != group & !is.na(Data.soft$Mixed_Group)]
      
      # Only test if both groups have enough participants
      if (length(group1) > 2 && length(group2) > 2) {
        test_result <- wilcox.test(group1, group2, exact = FALSE)
        
        p_values[var, group] <- test_result$p.value
        test_estimates[var, group] <- median(group1, na.rm = TRUE) - median(group2, na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    }
  }
}
get_significance <- function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}

significance <- matrix(sapply(p_values, get_significance), nrow = nrow(p_values))
rownames(test_estimates) <- pretty_names
rownames(significance) <- pretty_names

# Save heatmap as JPEG
png("Heatmap_of_4_mixed etiology.fixed.png", width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 600, bg = "white")
# Set matrix name to customize the color legend title
attr(test_estimates, "matrix_name") <- "Estimate"
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)

pheatmap(test_estimates, 
         cluster_rows = TRUE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE,
         scale = "row",
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         display_numbers = significance,
         color = my_palette,
         angle_col = "0",
         fontsize_row = 13,
         fontsize_col = 13,
         main = "Heatmap of Clinical Associations Across Mixed Etiology Groups")

dev.off()

```


#Revised mixed etiology only for clinical variables (using the Mann whiteny u test  (used this for publication)
```{r}
setwd(Sys.getenv("KORA_RUN_DIR"))
##Creating Heatmap of Mixed Etiology using the Mann whiteny u test 
# Load required library
library(pheatmap)
clinical_vars <- c("u3talteru", "u3tgewi", "u3tgroe", "u3tbmi", 
                   "u3twhrat", "u3tsysmm", "u3tdiamm", 
                   "u3tglukfastn", "u3tgluk2n", 
                   "u3tinsfastn", "u3tins2n", "u3tquickin",  
                   "u3lk_choln", "u3lk_hdln", "u3lk_ldln", "u3lk_trin", 
                   "u3lk_krean", "u3l_hbavn", "u3h_crp", "u3thoma2_ir", 
                   "u3thoma2_s", "u3thoma2_b")

pretty_names <- c(
  "Age", "Weight", "Height", "BMI", 
   "WHR",  "SBP", "DBP",
   "Fasting_glucose", "Glucose_2h",  
  "Fasting_serum_insulin", "Insulin_2h", "Insulin_Sensitivity_Quicki",
  "Cholesterol", "HDL", "LDL", "TG", "Creatinine", "HbA1c", "hsCRP", 
  "HOMA_IR", "HOMA_Sensitivity", "HOMA_Beta"
)
Data.soft$Mixed_Group <- NA
Data.soft$Mixed_Group[mixed_etiology] <- mixed_groups
test_estimates <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(clinical_vars), ncol = length(unique(mixed_groups)))
p_values <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(clinical_vars), ncol = length(unique(mixed_groups)))

rownames(test_estimates) <- clinical_vars
colnames(test_estimates) <- unique(mixed_groups)
rownames(p_values) <- clinical_vars
colnames(p_values) <- unique(mixed_groups)
for (group in unique(mixed_groups)) {
  group_indices <- which(Data.soft$Mixed_Group == group)
  
  for (var in clinical_vars) {
    if (!is.null(group_indices) && length(group_indices) > 0) {
      group1 <- Data.soft[[var]][Data.soft$Mixed_Group == group]
      group2 <- Data.soft[[var]][Data.soft$Mixed_Group != group & !is.na(Data.soft$Mixed_Group)]
      
      # Only test if both groups have enough participants
      if (length(group1) > 2 && length(group2) > 2) {
        test_result <- wilcox.test(group1, group2, exact = FALSE)
        
        p_values[var, group] <- test_result$p.value
        test_estimates[var, group] <- median(group1, na.rm = TRUE) - median(group2, na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    }
  }
}
get_significance <- function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  else if (p < 0.001) return("***")
  else if (p < 0.01) return("**")
  else if (p < 0.05) return("*")
  else return("")
}

significance <- matrix(sapply(p_values, get_significance), nrow = nrow(p_values))
rownames(test_estimates) <- pretty_names
rownames(significance) <- pretty_names

# Remove legend title
attr(test_estimates, "name") <- ""          # works in recent pheatmap
attr(test_estimates, "matrix_name") <- NULL # just in case you set it earlier

png("Heatmap_of_4_mixed etiology.fixed.png", width = 10,height = 8, units = "in", res = 600)
# Set matrix name to customize the color legend title
attr(test_estimates, "matrix_name") <- "Estimate"
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)

pheatmap(test_estimates, 
         cluster_rows = TRUE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE,
         scale = "row",
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = TRUE,
         display_numbers = significance,
         color = my_palette,
         angle_col = "0",
         fontsize_row = 13,
         fontsize_col = 13,
         main = "Heatmap of Clinical Associations Across Mixed Etiology Groups")

dev.off()
```

#Creatin a list to at the same time plotting all the boxplots together
```{r}

setwd(Sys.getenv("KORA_RUN_DIR"))

library(ggpubr)

# Define variables and their corresponding y-axis labels
boxplot_vars <- list(
  "u3tbmi" = "BMI",
  "u3tgewi" = "Weight",
  "u3twhrat" = "Waist-Hip Ratio",
  "u3tsysmm" = "Systolic Blood Pressure",
  "u3tdiamm" = "Diastolic Blood Pressure",
  "u3tglukfastn" = "Fasting Glucose",
  "u3tgluk2n" = "2 hours Glucose",
  "u3tinsfastn" = "Fasting Serum Insulin",
  "u3tins2n" = "2 hours Insulin",
  "u3thoma2_b" = "HOMA-Beta Cell Function",
  "u3thoma2_s" = "HOMA Insulin Sensitivity",
  "u3thoma2_ir" = "HOMA-Insulin Resistance",
  "u3tquickin" = "Quantitative Insulin Sensitivity Check Index",
  "u3lk_choln" = "Total Cholesterol",
  "u3lk_hdln" = "HDL",
  "u3lk_ldln" = "LDL",
  "u3lk_trin" = "Fasting Triglyceride",
  "u3lk_krean" = "Creatinine",
  "u3l_hbavn" = "Fasting HbA1c Value",
  "u3h_crp" = "High Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein",
  "u3tgroe" = "Height",
  "u3talteru" = "Age at Examination Date"
)

# Define color palette
color_palette <- c("red","blue", "lightgreen","purple","#E7B800", "#00AFBB","grey")

# Loop through variables and save plots
for (var in names(boxplot_vars)) {
  # Create the boxplot
  p <- ggboxplot(Data.soft, x = "Extreme_Archetype_Number", y = var,
                 color = "Extreme_Archetype_Number", palette = color_palette,
                 order = c("1", "2","3","4", "Mixed Etiology"),#adjust the number of archetypes here
                 ylab = boxplot_vars[[var]], xlab = "Archetype") +
       theme_minimal() +  # Use minimal theme for better visualization
       ggtitle(boxplot_vars[[var]]) +  # Add the title
       theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  # Center the title

  # Save each plot with a unique filename
  filename <- paste0("boxplot_", var, ".png")
  ggsave(filename, plot = p, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
}
```

```{r}
  labs(x = "Extreme Archetype Number", y = "Count",
```

```{r}
  "u3tinsfastn" = "Fasting Serum Insulin",
  "u3thoma2_b" = "HOMA-Beta Cell Function",

  "u3thoma2_ir" = "HOMA-Insulin Resistance",
  "u3tquickin" = "Quantitative Insulin Sensitivity Check Index",
  "u3lk_choln" = "Total Cholesterol",
  "u3lk_hdln" = "HDL",
  "u3lk_ldln" = "LDL",
  "u3lk_trin" = "Fasting Triglyceride",
  "u3lk_krean" = "Creatinine",
  "u3l_hbavn" = "Fasting HbA1c Value",
  "u3h_crp" = "High Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein",
  "u3tgroe" = "Height",
  "u3talteru" = "Age at Examination Date"
)

# Define improved color palette
color_palette <- c("red","blue", "lightgreen","purple","#E7B800", "#00AFBB","grey")

# Loop through variables and save violin plots
for (var in names(violin_vars)) {
  
  # Generate violin plot
  p <- ggplot(Data.soft, aes(x = as.factor(Extreme_Archetype_Number), y = get(var), 
                             fill = as.factor(Extreme_Archetype_Number))) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +  # Full distribution
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", color = "black", outlier.shape = NA) +  # Boxplot inside
    scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette, name =  "Archetypes") +  # Fix legend name
    labs(title = paste("Violin Plot of", violin_vars[[var]], "Across Archetypes"),
         x = "Archetypes", y = violin_vars[[var]]) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text( angle = 30, vjust = 1, hjust = 1, size = 10),#angle = 45,# Rotate x-axis labels
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, face = "bold"),  # Reduce title size
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),  # Adjust legend title size
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10)  # Adjust legend text size
    )

  # Save each plot with a unique filename
  filename <- paste0("violin_", var, ".png")
  ggsave(filename, plot = p, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
}
```

#Statistical analysis 

##Linear Regression
```{r}
# Define phenotypes
phenotypes <- setdiff(names(Data.soft), c("Extreme_Archetype_Number"))

# Function to run linear regression for each phenotype
run_regression <- function(phenotype) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(phenotype, "~ Extreme_Archetype_Number"))
  model <- tryCatch({
    lm(formula, data = Data.soft)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Error in regression for ", phenotype, ": ", e$message)
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (!is.null(model)) {
    tidy_result <- tryCatch({
      tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE)
    }, error = function(e) {
      message("Error in tidy for ", phenotype, ": ", e$message)
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    if (!is.null(tidy_result)) {
      tidy_result$phenotype <- phenotype
      return(tidy_result)
    }
  }
  return(NULL)
}

# Run regression for all phenotypes
results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(phenotypes, run_regression))


# Add adjusted p-values
results$p.adjusted <- p.adjust(results$p.value, method = "bonferroni")

# Sort results
results <- results %>%
  arrange(phenotype, p.value) %>%
  select(phenotype, term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, p.adjusted, conf.low, conf.high)

# View results
print(results)

# Save results to CSV
write.csv(results, "linear_regression_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Function to create boxplot for each phenotype
create_boxplot <- function(phenotype) {
  ggboxplot(Data.soft, x = "Extreme_Archetype_Number", y = phenotype,
            color = "Extreme_Archetype_Number", palette = c("#00AFBB","#FC4E07","#E7B800"),
            order = c("Mixed Etiology", "1", "2"),
            ylab = phenotype, xlab = "Archetype") +
    stat_compare_means(method = "anova")
}


# Create and save boxplots for each phenotype
for (phenotype in phenotypes) {
  plot <- create_boxplot(phenotype)
  ggsave(paste0("boxplot_", phenotype, ".png"), plot, width = 10, height = 6)
}

# Summary of significant associations
significant_results <- results %>%
  filter(p.adjusted < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(p.adjusted)

print(significant_results)
write.csv(significant_results,"Regression_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)


##
```


##Wilcoxon Test 
```{r}
# Initialize results data frame for Wilcoxon tests
wilcox_results <- data.frame(variable = character(), p_value = numeric(), statistic = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Loop through each variable in Data.soft except 'assignments' and 'group'
for (var in colnames(Data.soft)[!colnames(Data.soft) %in% c("Extreme_Archetype_Number")]) {
  # Perform Wilcoxon test
  test_result <- wilcox.test(Data.soft[[var]] ~ Data.soft$Extreme_Archetype_Number, 
                             exact = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")
  
  # Store results in the data frame
  wilcox_results <- rbind(wilcox_results, 
                          data.frame(variable = var, 
                                     p_value = test_result$p.value, 
                                     statistic = test_result$statistic))
}

# View Wilcoxon test results
print(wilcox_results)

write.csv(wilcox_results, "wilcox_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

##Kruskal-Wallis test

##For comparing more than two groups Kruskal-Wallis test is used 
##Kruskal-Wallis test by rank is a non-parametric alternative to one-way ANOVA test, which extends the two-samples Wilcoxon test in the situation where there are more than two groups. It’s recommended when the assumptions of one-way ANOVA test are not met
#Performing for the whole data together If the archetypes are 

```{r}
# Show the group levels
levels(Data.soft$Extreme_Archetype_Number)

#Defining phenotype
phenotypes <- Data.soft[, setdiff(names(Data.soft), c("Extreme_Archetype_Number"))]

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis tests
kruskal_test <- function(phenotype) {
  test_result <- kruskal.test(phenotype ~ Extreme_Archetype_Number, data = Data.soft)
  return(c(statistic = test_result$statistic, p.value = test_result$p.value))
}

# Apply the function to each phenotype
results <- sapply(phenotypes, kruskal_test)

# Convert results to a data frame
results_df <- as.data.frame(t(results))
results_df$phenotype <- rownames(results_df)
rownames(results_df) <- NULL

# Add adjusted p-values
results_df$p.adjusted <- p.adjust(results_df$p.value, method = "bonferroni")

# Sort results by p-value
results_df <- results_df[order(results_df$p.value), ]

# View the results
print(results_df)

# Optionally, save the results
write.csv(results_df, "kruskal_wallis_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
